subject.title: [Feature/RFC]: Add eval-backed option discovery to avoid premature convergence in route/strategy answers

question: Should OpenClaw adopt eval-backed option discovery before confident route, strategy, or choice recommendations as a default invariant, or keep it as opt-in research behavior?
rationale: The evidence shows a credible user-trust gap and absent current contract, but making this default affects runtime behavior, tool usage, latency, and Codex prompt-surface ownership.

options.title: Adopt eval-first default invariant
options.body: Accept the invariant only after a generic QA Lab scenario proves neighboring-option discovery without incident-specific literals, then add the narrow shared prompt/runtime contract.

options.title: Keep it opt-in
options.body: Treat deeper option discovery as a research or best-insight profile so default answers stay lean and lower-latency.

options.title: Reject for now
options.body: Close the default-behavior request until maintainers have a deterministic live repro or stronger demand signal beyond the redacted incident.

recommendation.title: Adopt eval-first default invariant
recommendation.body: Accept the invariant only after a generic QA Lab scenario proves neighboring-option discovery without incident-specific literals, then add the narrow shared prompt/runtime contract.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a product/default-behavior scope choice more than a single-file repair, and current routing evidence points to broad maintainer review rather than one contributor-owned patch.
